item.content:encoded:
Has the potential to be a bit cliche, but it's done well for the most part. That being said, the most interesting portions of it have been expunged! I understand why, given that it's SCP personnel being discussed, and the vagueness adds an air of mystery to it, but it is still a bit disappointing. That the nature of the calls changes around family-oriented holidays like Thanksgiving or Christmas is another very unique aspect of it, and one that helps it stand out a bit.

I wonder if the nature of the calls would change around Valentine's Day? It's a time that has an awful lot of people thinking about their interpersonal relationships, after all.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really dislike the execution of this one. The concept isn't bad, but little of real interest is done with it, the writing is sketchy, and the formatting is bad in a few places, like the 'Nature Of Call'. That's not a very indicative way to describe that. I think breaking into two sections would have been better: Identity Of Caller and Content Of Call.

In-depth critique
I swear I will stop wall of texting eventually

SCP-467 appears to be an empty phone booth, and was found in [DATA EXPUNGED]. The SCP Foundation discovered it due to a legend about a 'haunted phone' that used to reside inside the booth, although testing has revealed that the phone was of no importance, and the effects came from the booth itself. Even after the phone was removed, the booth itself remained a place of superstition before being recovered by [DATA EXPUNGED].

I'm turned off by this part immediately because of the awful expungement. Neither of these should be an expunge, blackboxing would be far more appropriate.

Although there is nothing extraordinary about the booth itself, so long as a human and a communications device are in the booth at the same time, its effects are easily observed.

If it's so clear that it has supernatural effects, there is something extraordinary about the booth. This is just poor wording though.

Subject: Class D personnel; [DATA EXPUNGED]
Nature of Call: [DATA EXPUNGED]
Effects: Violent outbursts intermittent with hysterical sobbing. Subject was terminated after an attack on nearby researchers.

Zero information. No hints. Awful expunge. Remove this entire test and nothing changes.

Subject: SCP-1599
Nature of Call: Message from subject's creator or creators claiming they have lost its signal, don't know where it has gone, and that they are unable to recover it.
Effects: Subject denied the message came from its creator, and believed the message was a trick performed by its captors.

Despite this having come from a staff edit, I REALLY dislike this addition. Crosslinks are awesome, but the article explicitly says "so long as a human and a communications device are in the booth at the same time". This either needs to be rewritten to allow for non-human sapient entities, or the crosslink needs to be pulled. This one test alone is enough to destroy an already weak scip with this.

Subject: Dr. Rights
Nature of Call: Unknown.
Effects: Moderate depression for approximately two days, intermittent with doubt regarding working with the Foundation. Full recovery followed.

Subject: Dr. Iceberg
Nature of Call: Unknown
Effects: No immediate effects. Two days later began an argument with a researcher at Site 17, which lead to a mild physical conflict. Full reprimand followed.

Why are these 'Unknown'? Poor documentation, poor research - if you're going to NOT say what's going on with these calls because they're coming from Foundation staff, give literally any indication of why - the doctors refused to clarify, or shut off the recording devices(as with later test entry), something.

Incident Report - ██/██/██ Near holidays such as Thanksgiving and Christmas, a notable increase in disturbing or distressing calls has been observed. Theory currently holds that this is due to increased family tension and urges to be 'nice' to people at this point in time. Additionally, it was during the holiday season that the first two reported incidents occured of occupant inside SCP-467 receiving a call from themselves, and other reported incidents of an occupant receiving a call from the deceased or non-existent. Further investigation pending on how personnel could 'lie' to themselves, and how SCP-467 receives calls from non-existing sources.

Feels redundant to have this entire paragraph saying this. I'd much prefer brief researcher notes after the questionable tests noting "This was the first time we've seen someone call themselves". As for the holidays, there's zero followup testing to really indicate that, so again, kinda redundant.

Subject: Secretarial/Security Staff Break
Nature of Call: Dr. Iceberg [REDACTED].
Effects: [REDACTED]

Zero information. Zero point. Bad redaction.

Subject: Dr. Rights
Nature of Call: Voice was described as that of a young child; Dr. Rights shut off the recording equipment after voice revealed to belong to [DATA EXPUNGED].
Effects: [DATA EXPUNGED]

This one? This is perfect expungement. That's EXACTLY the purpose of expungement. It actually makes the rest of the poor redaction worse because someone clearly got it RIGHT in here.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as described below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, here we have a phone booth that puts people in contact with those they know to get dealt a whammy of a confession. We just so happen to have multiple SCPs on the site where a big part of the article has been that they have lost contact with their creator/creators, of these SCP-1599 is notable. As such, I am proposing the following addition to the testing log.

Subject: SCP-1599
Nature of Call: Message from subject's creator or creators claiming they have lost its signal, don't know where it has gone, and that they are unable to recover it.
Effects: Subject denied the message came from its creator, and believed the message was a trick performed by its captors.

Such a log not only adds a little flavor to SCP-1599's backstory, but also sheds light on the power of SCP-467, since its strongly implied in its own article that SCP-1599 has extra-dimensional origins. I'd argue placing it before the incident report in the test log stream.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Not the most thought-provoking of SCPs but I like it. Simple, weird and with lots of potential. One thing that I feel should be mentioned yet isn't is whether the confessions are always true? Considering calls occasionally come from the same person receiving them or from non-existent people, it seems like it wouldn't be the case, but the article gives the impression that it is.

Another detail I find weird is the two D-Class people being immediately terminated when trying to destroy SCP-467. Does the Foundation not have non-lethal methods of neutralizing a test subject? Even if they don't care about killing D-Class (a concept I never liked as it makes the SCP Foundation evil for evil's sake when at most they should be a necessary evil), I would have thought they would want to interview them after the fact and besides, using lethal force is taking a risk of damaging SCP-467, which beats the purpose of "terminating" the D-Class for attempting to damage SCP-467.

Finally, I find this bit odd:

It is suggested that the booth not be used for personal reasons.

The receiver does not appear to be able to influence the kind of messages they receive (or if they do, they don't do it consciously) so how could they use it for personal reasons?

But nitpicking aside, I like it and I think the test logs really add to it.
